newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A number of foreign delegates and journalists in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit next month have been marked for assasination by local leftist groups, an intelligence official said yesterday (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Wage increases ranging from 17 to 50 pesos have been proposed by the government's economic planning chief and several congressmen to enable workers' families to cope with rising prices of basic goods. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)
- German chancellor Helmut Kohl arrives in Manila for a three-day visit aimed at strengthening trade between the Philippines and its most important European trading partner (TODAY)

- Filipino Catholic bishops supported a plan of the organisers of a parallel forum to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit to invite East Timor bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo in place of resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Philippine National Bank president Peter Favila remains optimistic that the bank will meet its revised net income projection of 1.7 billion pesos by yearend. (STAR)
- The Philippines remains on the watchlist of the United States for violations of the intellectual property rights. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
